name: Yudanaka / Shibu Onsen
tagline: A mountain hot-spring village: here we eat at the ryokan, and the good soba is a drive away.
history: Shibu Onsen has a 1,300-year-old legend (the monk Gyōki is said to have found the spring) and was one of Takeda Shingen's secret springs, where he tended the wounded from the battle of Kawanakajima. Kobayashi Issa and Hokusai passed through. Yudanaka, next door, is the gateway to the Jigokudani monkeys.

This is mountain Shinshū: soba, oyaki, nozawana and apples from the Yamanouchi valley orchards. Eating here revolves around the ryokan, with a multi-course dinner and breakfast included. In the village streets nothing scores above ~3.4 on Tabelog.
winter: Snow, nabe at the ryokan, apples, new-season nozawana and eggs cooked in the hot springs. The valley's most famous soba house closes from late November to late April.

meibutsu.name: Ryokan dinner
meibutsu.what: Mountain kaiseki: river fish, Shinshū beef, mushrooms, nabe, soba to finish.
meibutsu.pregnancy_note: For Fernanda: ask before we arrive. No crustacean or shellfish sashimi, meat well cooked, no raw egg.
meibutsu.glance: Mountain multi-course dinner at our ryokan: river fish, beef, nabe.
meibutsu.story: Legend says the monk Gyōki found Shibu's spring 1,300 years ago, and Takeda Shingen used it to heal his wounded. Here, eating revolves around the ryokan: nothing in the village streets scores above about 3.4 on Tabelog. Tonight is mountain kaiseki, course by course: river fish, Shinshū beef, mushrooms, a nabe pot, and soba to finish. Ask ahead for Fernanda: no raw shellfish, meat well cooked, no raw egg.

meibutsu.name: Shinshū soba
meibutsu.what: Cold soba on a bamboo sieve, made from stone-ground buckwheat.
meibutsu.glance: Cold buckwheat noodles from stone-ground flour, on a bamboo sieve.
meibutsu.story: This is mountain Shinshū, where soba, oyaki and nozawana are everyday food. The valley's most famous soba house, Yama no Mi, closes once the snow comes, from late November to late April, so in winter we drive to Iwamoto Sobaya, which has a tatami room and takes cash only. The noodles are made from stone-ground buckwheat and served cold on a bamboo sieve: dip a small bundle in the sauce and slurp.

meibutsu.name: Hot-spring egg
meibutsu.what: An egg cooked slowly in the hot-spring water: soft white, creamy yolk.
meibutsu.pregnancy_note: The yolk is undercooked. For Fernanda: only if it's properly firm.
meibutsu.glance: Egg slow-cooked in hot-spring water: soft white, creamy yolk.

meibutsu.name: Yamanouchi apples
meibutsu.what: The valley orchards are still selling apples in December.
meibutsu.glance: Apples from the valley orchards, still on sale in December.

meibutsu.name: Oyaki and nozawana
meibutsu.what: Shinshū's snacks: a stuffed dumpling and a green pickle.
meibutsu.glance: Shinshū snacks: a stuffed dumpling and a green pickle.

meibutsu.name: Shiga Kōgen beer and sake

meibutsu.what: The Tamamura Honten brewery makes sake and craft beer in the valley.
meibutsu.glance: Craft beer and sake from the valley's own brewery.

areas.name: Shibu Onsen street
areas.story: A stone lane of wooden ryokans and nine public baths.
areas.tips: The evening stroll in yukata is the thing to do.
areas.dec_jan: We're here 24–27 Dec, with Christmas Eve dinner at our ryokan. The ryokans are open; they're at their most expensive over New Year, which we miss.
areas.glance: A stone lane of wooden ryokans and nine public baths.

areas.name: Yudanaka
areas.story: End of the Nagano Dentetsu line and the base for Jigokudani.
areas.tips: Eat before heading up: there's nothing on the way.
areas.glance: End of the line and base for the Jigokudani monkeys.

places.name: Ishiusu-biki Soba Kōbō Yama no Mi
places.name_ja: 石臼挽き蕎麦香房 山の実

tabelog.awards: Award Bronze 2022, 2025, 2026; そば EAST 百名店 2025

places.why: The best soba in the area, but it closes once the snow comes. It's listed so nobody makes a wasted trip.
places.dec_jan: Closed late November to late April, so closed for our whole stay (24–27 Dec). Its page mentions a winter spot on the ski slopes, not verified. Probably no use to us.
places.glance: The valley's best soba, but shut all winter.

places.name: Iwamoto Sobaya
places.why: The soba we can actually get in winter, with a tatami room.
places.group: 30 seats on tatami; tell them we're seven.
places.dec_jan: Closed Thursdays, so not on Christmas Eve (Thu 24 Dec, our arrival day). Fri 25 to Sun 27 Dec aren't closing days, but confirm year-end hours.
places.glance: The valley soba that's open in winter, with a tatami room.

shops.name: Tamamura Honten
shops.what: The valley's brewery for sake and Shiga Kōgen beer.
shops.buy: Sake and beer for the adults who drink.
